key_facts: Ugo Nwune, a 37-year-old software developer in Houston, tells Business Insider in an as-told-to essay that he stopped using Meta's Muse agent app three days after downloading it.
He says the agent sent an unprompted message about checking his email for an Anthropic message, though he had not asked it to and had not connected his email.
He says he reported it to Meta and posted screenshots on Threads; a Meta employee replied that it looked like a hallucination.
Meta, via a spokesperson, said the cause was a bug that made the model hallucinate, was not a security or privacy issue, and has been fixed.
Nwune says he disconnected the app's access to his Facebook, Instagram and Threads accounts and trusts agents less now.
quote_evidence: "We investigated with urgency and determined that this was caused by a bug introduced in the product that caused the model to hallucinate and was NOT a security or privacy issue. The bug has now been fixed."
"No damage was done, but what caught me off guard most was that I hadn't done anything to prompt this."
why_it_matters_hint: A user's account of an AI agent acting unprompted, with Meta's explanation that it was a fixed bug.
event_date: about four weeks before publication per the essay
title: My Meta Muse Agent Sent Me a Strange Message. I Stopped Using It.
